questions.s:
A student measures the rate of the reaction between marble chips, CaCO3, and dilute hydrochloric acid.
CaCO3 + 2HCl → CaCl2 + CO2 + H2O
Which diagrams show the apparatus that are suitable for this experiment?

Chromatograms of a urine sample using two different solvents are shown below.
Based on the two chromatograms, which drug(s) is/are present in the urine sample?

Since the discovery of graphite, scientists have been able to extract a single layer of carbon atoms (known as graphene) and convert it to another material known as graphane by attaching one hydrogen atom to each carbon atom as shown below.
Which property of graphene is not likely to be shared by graphane?
o: It has a high melting point.

questions.s:
An isotope of element Z has 20 neutrons and 17 protons.
Which is the correct symbol for an ion of the isotope of element Z?

Hydrogen is able to form compounds with metals and non-metals. The formulae of some of these compounds are shown below.
CH4   HCl   MgH2   KH
What is the order of melting point of these compounds? (lowest melting point → highest melting point)

The heating curves (not drawn to scale) of nitrogen and oxygen over a period of time are shown in the graph.
At which temperature will there be two different states of matter co-existing at the same time, in a mixture of nitrogen and oxygen under similar conditions?

The diagram below shows the bonding between P and Q in the covalent molecule, PQ2.
What are the electronic structures of atoms P and Q before combining together to form the above molecule?

0.1 mole of a chloride XCl2 combines with 10.8 g of water to form the hydrated salt, XCl2.nH2O.
What is the value of n?

Ammonia reacts with chlorine according to the equation shown below:
2NH3 (g) + 3Cl2 (g) → N2 (g) + 6HCl (g)
If 90 cm3 of ammonia is mixed with 60 cm3 of Cl2 and all the volumes were measured at room temperature and pressure, what is the total volume of gases at the end of the reaction?

When 4.8 g of magnesium is heated in a crucible, 5.9 g of magnesium oxide is formed.
What is the percentage yield of magnesium oxide?

A student is given two samples, one of which is aluminium oxide and the other is magnesium carbonate. He needs to find a method to identify the two samples.
Which of the following show(s) the correct method(s) and observation(s)?
methodobservation(s)
1add nitric acidonly aluminium oxide dissolves
2add nitric acidboth samples dissolve. Effervescence is observed in the reaction with magnesium carbonate
3add sodium hydroxideonly aluminium oxide dissolves
4add sodium hydroxideboth samples dissolve. Effervescence is observed in both the reactions

pH rangecolour
0 – 3violet
4 – 8blue
9 – 11green
12 – 14yellow
Which pair of substances can be distinguished by adding butterfly pea flower extract to each substance separately?

A student stated that since low temperatures produce a greater yield of ammonia, the reaction should be carried out at 50 °C instead of 450 °C.
Which statement best explains why the reaction is not carried out at 50 °C?
o: The reaction is too slow at 50 °C.
The reaction mixture is easily separated at higher temperatures.

questions.s:
Ammonium chloride is heated strongly in a boiling tube. Damp blue and red litmus papers were placed at the mouth of the boiling tube for the gases produced.
Which row shows the correct sequence of observations that would be made?
o: first observed colour change: the damp blue litmus paper turns red; final colour of both litmus papers: red
first observed colour change: the damp blue litmus paper turns red then bleaches; final colour of both litmus papers: white
first observed colour change: the damp red litmus paper turns blue; final colour of both litmus papers: blue
first observed colour change: the damp red litmus paper turns blue; final colour of both litmus papers: red

questions.s:
Which are redox reactions?
1   HCl + NaOH → NaCl + H2O
2   Zn + 2HNO3 → Zn(NO3)2 + H2
3   Ag2SO4 + 2NaCl → 2AgCl + Na2SO4
4   2Fe2+ + Cl2 → 2Fe3+ + 2Cl−

Dry hydrogen gas is passed over a heated brown powdered solid and then through a cooled U-tube before the excess of hydrogen is burned in air.
A colourless liquid collects in the U-tube. What could the brown powdered solid be?

Equal masses of different metals 1 to 4 are placed in the test tubes containing an equal volume of hydrochloric acid of equal concentration.
The thermometers show the maximum temperature recorded for the reaction. (The room temperature is 25 °C.)
Which statements are most likely to be true?
I   Metal 3 will displace metals 2 and 4 from their aqueous salt solutions.
II   Metal 2 can likely be extracted by chemical reduction of its oxide by carbon.
III   Metal 1 is likely to be obtained by electrolysing its molten chloride.

The energy profile diagram represents a chemical reaction carried out with a catalyst and without a catalyst.
What is the enthalpy change for the catalysed reaction?

Hydrogen peroxide reacts with potassium iodide in the presence of dilute acid to produce iodine molecules as shown in the equation below.
H2O2 (aq) + 2I− (aq) + 2H+ (aq) → I2 (aq) + 2H2O (l)
Which factor would not affect the rate of this reaction?
o: Temperature of the reacting vessel and its surroundings

questions.s:

2H2O2 → 2H2O + O2
Which change to the original experimental conditions would produce curve 2?
o: adding some 0.1 mol/dm<sup>3</sup> hydrogen peroxide solution

questions.s: In which set-up will the bulb light up?

During an electrolysis, X+ and Y− ions are selectively discharged as shown in the equations below:
Cathode: 2X+ + 2e− → X2
Anode: 2Y− → Y2 + 2e−
What can the electrolyte be?
In which electrolysis experiment would there be no change in the concentration of the solution?
o: electrodes: carbon; electrolyte: aqueous copper(II) sulfate
electrodes: copper; electrolyte: aqueous copper(II) sulfate
electrodes: carbon; electrolyte: concentrated potassium chloride
electrodes: platinum; electrolyte: dilute sulfuric acid

questions.s:
Methane reacts very slowly with air at room temperature. However, if a transition metal T is added to the methane-air mixture, the methane ignites quickly.
A student made some statements about the observation.
I   Addition of T reduces the activation energy.
II   Addition of T increases the enthalpy change.
III   Addition of T increases the rate of reaction.
IV   Addition of T reduces the energy of the reactants.
Which statements are correct?

The positions of the elements W, X, Y and Z are shown in part of the periodic table.
Which statement is not correct?
o: All the elements are reactive except for element Z.
Element W and element Y can form ionic bonds.
Element X will react with element Z in the ratio 1:2.
Element Y and element Z will form a compound by sharing electrons.

questions.s: Which statement is not true when chlorine gas is bubbled into potassium iodide solution?
o: Chlorine is more reactive than iodine and hence displaces iodine form potassium iodide solution.
Potassium iodide is the reducing agent.
The ionic equation for the reaction is Cl2(g) + 2I−(aq) → 2Cl−(aq) + I2(aq)
The solution turns from brown to colourless.

questions.s:
Bioethanol can be obtained from the fermentation of the sugar in sugarcane.
Which statement best explains why burning of bioethanol is considered more environmentally sustainable compared to the use of fossil fuels?
o: As sugarcane grows, it absorbs carbon dioxide produced during photosynthesis.
Cabon dioxide and water are formed during burning of bioethanol.
Sugarcane plants can be regrown and replaced within a short period of time.
Sugarcane plants need to be planted and transported for treatment.

o: The molecules in fraction X contain more carbon atoms than the molecules in fraction Y.
The molecules in fraction X are more flammable than the molecules in fraction Y.
The molecules in fraction X are larger than the molecules in fraction Y.
The molecules in fraction X have higher boiling points than the molecules in fraction Y.

Which structures are isomers?

The diagram below shows an organic compound, cysteine.
Which statement about cysteine is true?
o: Effervescence is observed when magnesium metal is added to cysteine.
It forms a polymer with the same linkage as terylene.
It forms an addition polymer with other units of cysteine.
